text:
miko: Heads-up — thinking about a small refactor to the model intake flow so compatibility checks run earlier and cheaper. Two goals: avoid heavy bench runs for obviously incompatible models, and give faster feedback to model owners.

tara: +1, been annoyed by multi-hour bench queues where the fail is a simple dtype mismatch. What's the proposed gate ordering?

miko: sketch: 1) quick metadata lint (shapes, dtype, ops list) 2) lightweight runtime probe (tiny infer with KV/seq=16) 3) compatibility heuristic (onnx/pt graph parity) 4) full bench only if passes 2-3.

sam: how lightweight is the "runtime probe"? We need to catch memory blowups and OOM regressions too.

miko: probe is <10s, single-batch, low-seq. Run on a cheap test node, not full GPU pool. If probe OOMs -> mark as "needs-quant" or "structural-fix" and skip bench.

tara: Will that block models that require custom ops? We sometimes accept those with a shim.

miko: we add an opt-in flag in intake metadata: "custom_ops": [..] so probe knows to expect shims. If flagged, probe runs a shim validation step rather than strict parity.

sam: What about golden input coverage? Full bench uses golden prompts, but early probes might miss generation-specific failures.

miko: agree — probe is compliment, not replacement. We still run golden-smoke in the bench stage. But we gate expensive sampling + latency SLO tests behind a pass. That should reduce wasted bench cycles.

juniper-bot: PR created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ml-intake/pulls/834 — contains the probe harness and new metadata schema. CI: quick-probe workflow added. :rocket:

tara: Nice. A few nitpicks: 1) need clear error codes from probe so automation can map to remediation templates (e.g., "dtype-mismatch", "oom", "op-missing"). 2) add explicit retry/backoff for transient infra failures.

miko: noted. I'll map probe failures -> machine-readable codes. Backoff: probe will attempt 2 tries spaced 30s, then escalate.

sam: For the compatibility heuristic (graph parity), can we reuse existing conversion tooling rather than inventing another comparator? Maybe call converter --dry-run and parse exit codes.

miko: yes, plan is to call our existing converter with `--dry-run --strict-shape-check`. If exit code 0 -> pass, 1 -> convertible-with-warnings, 2 -> fail. We'll surface this in intake UI.

tara: How do we measure cost savings? Want a dashboard showing bench-hours avoided, and median time-to-feedback improvement.

miko: will add metrics: `intake.probe_pass_rate`, `intake.bench_skips`, `intake.mean_feedback_seconds`. Also tag by `model_family` and `custom_ops` to analyze hotspots.

sam: One more: rolling this out as a canary — first enable for internal teams only, then opt-in on external onboarding. Also, add a fallback route where maintainers can request a full bench despite a probe failure (manual override).

miko: agreed. Canary plan: 2 weeks internal -> metrics review -> opt-in for orgs -> default-on after 6 weeks. Manual override via intake UI + audit log entry.

tara: Sounds good. Can we include a simple snippet in docs showing how to mark a model as intentionally large/fragile? e.g.:
```
metadata:
  name: giant-v2
  custom_ops: ["gpu-only-op"]
  expected_min_vram_gb: 38
  intake_flags: ["allow-slow-start"]
```

miko: will add to docs. I'll also add a short playbook for triaging probe failures and templates for common remediations.

juniper-bot: Action items assigned: miko (probe codes + PR followup), tara (metrics dashboard), sam (canary rollout plan). Due: next Wed.

miko: thanks. If anyone wants to complain about the name "probe" vs "smoke" feel free to bikeshed in thread :grimacing:

tara: :thumbsup: no bikeshedding, just results.

sam: LGTM.

miko: closing loop — will merge PR after tests, post rollout schedule in #eng-ml.
